text.p: Japan announced on Monday an $11.5 million donation to modernise Lima hospitals and provide electricity in remote regions, reaffirming its ties with Peru following a hostage crisis at its ambassador's home.

"With these donations the Japanese government wants to give testimony to its decision to continue to help the development of Peru, after the hostage crisis, through programmes to improve social infrastructure," a Japanese Embassy statement said.

A 126-day hostage siege ended on April 22 when Peruvian troops rescued 71 of 72 hostages held by Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels. Two commandos and all 14 rebels died in the raid launched from tunnels under the house.

Tokyo's donation included $7.2 million for hospitals in the capital Lima and $4.3 million for energy in the interior of Peru. Japan's goverment "wants to express its intention to continue and strengthen the friendship and cooperation between the two countries," the embassy statement said.

The Marxist rebels' main demand in the standoff was for the release of its jailed comrades, but the MRTA also used the siege to protest against poverty in Peru and Tokyo's "meddling" in the country's management.
